documents.title: New Patient Visit - Establish Care
documents.body:
Chief complaint: establishing care, headaches, 'my cholesterol was high before.'

HPI: Moved to Southampton from Lowell this spring with her wife. Last PCP visit 2017 at a practice in Lowell. Headaches since about age 15: unilateral, usually L temple, throbbing, nausea, light and sound sensitive, worse around menses. No visual or sensory aura. Lasts most of a day if untreated. Currently 4-5 headache days a month. Takes Excedrin 2 tabs, works 'about half the time.' Never tried a prescription med. Misses no work but drives the route 'squinting.' No thunderclap onset, no change in pattern, no nocturnal awakening, no neuro sx.
Lipids: told LDL was 162 in 2017, advised diet; no meds. No recheck since.

PMH: migraine as above. No surgeries. G0.
Meds: Excedrin PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father first MI at 51, died 2016 of a second MI. Mother HTN and type 2 DM (Lowell, lives with her brother). Sister with migraines. No colon/breast cancer known.
SH: born in Cambodia, came to Lowell age 4. Package-delivery driver x 20 yrs, 10-hr days, heavy lifting. Married to Sophea (police officer). Never smoker, rare wine, no drugs. Walks the dog most evenings. Diet: rice-based, eats on the route.

ROS: neg for chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, wt change, bowel or urinary changes. Menses regular q28d. Mood good.

Exam: BP 118/76, HR 72, BMI 26.0. Well appearing. HEENT nl, fundi sharp discs bilat. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft NT. No edema. Neuro: CN II-XII intact, strength 5/5, reflexes 2+ symmetric, gait nl.

A/P:
1. Migraine without aura, episodic, 4-5 days/mo. Normal neuro exam, stable lifelong pattern, no red flags; no imaging. Start sumatriptan 50 mg at onset, may repeat x1 at 2 h. Discussed limiting Excedrin/triptan to <10 days/mo to avoid medication-overuse headache. Headache diary. Triptan ok with driving once headache resolved; do not drive if drowsy.
2. Hyperlipidemia. Fasting lipid panel, CMP. Father with premature CAD. If LDL remains >160 we will discuss statin.
3. Health maintenance: Tdap today. Screening mammogram ordered (first). Pap due - will do at follow-up. HCV and HIV screening once - ordered. A1c and TSH with labs. Colon screening not yet due.

RTC 3 months, sooner prn.

R. Halvorsen, MD

documents.title: cholesterol question
documents.body: Hi Dr Halvorsen, I saw my cholesterol is still high. My dad had his heart attack young so honestly it scares me a little. Should I just start the pill now instead of waiting? I eat a lot of rice and I'm in the truck all day so I dont know how much I can change. Thanks, Sreymom

documents.title: RE: cholesterol question
documents.body: Hi Sreymom - very reasonable question, and given your dad's history a statin is on the table. Your 10-year risk is low right now, so a few months of trying first is safe. Small swaps help: brown rice or half-and-half, fewer fried snacks on the route, walking the dog you're already doing. If the LDL is still over 160 in December I'd recommend starting a statin, and you can decide then. - Dr. Halvorsen

documents.title: RE: propranolol
documents.body: Hi Sreymom, covering for Dr. Halvorsen today. Those numbers are expected on propranolol and are safe as long as you are not dizzy, lightheaded or short of breath. Tiredness often eases after the first month. Drink plenty of water on the route and stand up slowly. If you feel faint, or your heart rate is under 50, call us. Keep the diary going and we'll review at your next visit. - Jonah Petrakis, FNP

documents.body:
CC: establish care. 'My doctor in Lowell retired.'

HPI: 45F patrol officer, moved to Southampton 2019 with her wife (my pt), kept her long-time Lowell PCP until his retirement this summer. COPD diagnosed 2018 on spirometry after a winter of bronchitis; on tiotropium daily, albuterol ~2x/wk, mostly with exertion (stairs, foot pursuits, carrying gear). Morning cough, clear sputum. One flare 2019 treated at urgent care with an oral steroid burst; no hospitalizations. Smoking since 16, about a pack a day, more on overnight shifts. Has tried cold turkey twice, longest 3 weeks. Not sure she is ready - 'this job.' Can climb 2 flights without stopping.

PMH: COPD. Fertility care in Boston 2010-2011 (IUI with donor sperm); pregnancy 2011 ended in miscarriage at ~9 wk, passed without D&C. Couple stopped trying in 2012. G1P0010. No surgeries.
Meds: tiotropium Respimat 2.5 mcg 2 inh daily; albuterol HFA prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father died 2009 lung cancer (smoker). Mother COPD and type 2 DM, Lowell. Sister healthy. No colon or breast cancer.
SH: married to Sreymom since 2015. Police officer x16 yrs (Boston area 14 yrs, now a Hampshire County town department), rotating shifts. 3-4 beers/wk. No drugs. Firearm at home for work, stored in safe.
GYN: LMP 2 wk ago, cycles regular. Last Pap 2017 per pt, last mammogram 2019 (Lowell).

ROS: no hemoptysis, wt loss, night sweats, chest pain, edema. Bowels regular. Mood ok.

Exam: BP 124/80, HR 84, SpO2 95%, BMI 26.7. No distress, speaks full sentences. Nicotine stain R index finger. Heart RRR. Lungs: mildly decreased breath sounds bilat, scattered end-expiratory wheeze, prolonged expiration. No clubbing. Abd soft NT. No edema.

A/P:
1. COPD, by history GOLD 2 per pt; prior records requested. On LAMA, symptoms mild-moderate. Office spirometry at next visit. Inhaler technique reviewed - ok. Continue tiotropium, albuterol prn.
2. Tobacco dependence, ~27 pk-yr. Advised quitting clearly; pre-contemplative to contemplative. Offered varenicline/NRT and the state quitline; will think about it.
3. HCM: CBC with diff, CMP, lipids, A1c, HCV, HIV. Colorectal screening now recommended from 45 - she prefers colonoscopy, will refer when her shifts allow. Mammogram order placed. Pap due - schedule. Flu in fall; pneumococcal vaccine to be addressed.

RTC 6-8 wk with spirometry.

reports.text:
Office spirometry, pre- and post-bronchodilator (albuterol 360 mcg). Effort and reproducibility acceptable (ATS grade A).

Post: FVC 3.30 L (90%), FEV1 2.09 L (71%), FEV1/FVC 0.63. FEV1 change +80 mL (+4%), not significant.

documents.title: Colonoscopy
documents.body:
Indication: average-risk colorectal cancer screening, age 46.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care, propofol. ASA II (COPD, tobacco).
Prep: Boston Bowel Prep Scale 8 (3-3-2).
Procedure: Scope advanced to cecum, identified by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve; terminal ileum intubated. Withdrawal time 11 min.
Findings:
- 4 mm sessile polyp, mid transverse colon, removed with cold snare, retrieved.
- Moderate diverticulosis of the sigmoid colon, scattered descending colon diverticula. No inflammation or bleeding.
- Small non-bleeding internal hemorrhoids on retroflexion.
- Otherwise normal mucosa.
Complications: none. SpO2 nadir 93% on 2 L, recovered.
Impression: transverse polyp removed; sigmoid diverticulosis.
Plan: await pathology; repeat interval per histology. High-fiber diet. Resume regular diet.
S. Okafor, MD, Gastroenterology

documents.title: Colonoscopy pathology
documents.body:
Path from 8/23 colonoscopy: one 4 mm tubular adenoma, no HGD. GI recommends repeat colonoscopy in 7-10 years (2029-2032). Sigmoid diverticulosis - discussed fiber 25-30 g/day, fluids; nuts/seeds are fine. Called pt, she understood. Recall entered for 2029.
R. Halvorsen, MD

documents.title: Rooming and vaccines
documents.body:
Annual. VS per flowsheet, SpO2 95%. Smoking ~10/day. Flu IIV4 L deltoid, bivalent COVID booster R deltoid, VIS given, no reaction at 15 min. Mammogram order given - pt has not scheduled the one from last year.
- K. Dubois, CMA

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.body:
Interval: COVID 1/2022 on Paxlovid, recovered. Varenicline started 3/2022, cut down to 3-4/day; stopped it in May. Relapsed to ~10/day in July after a difficult call at work. Colonoscopy 8/23: tubular adenoma, sigmoid diverticulosis. Breathing: baseline, albuterol 1-2x/wk, no flares this year.
ROS: no chest pain, hemoptysis, wt loss. Bowels regular, no abd pain. Menses regular.
Meds: tiotropium Respimat daily, albuterol prn.
SH: married, patrol officer, rotating shifts. Beer 3-4/wk.

Exam: BP 126/80, HR 84, BMI 27.1. Well. Breasts: no masses or nodes. Lungs: decreased BS, mild end-exp wheeze. Heart RRR. Abd soft NT. Skin nl.

A/P:
1. Preventive: flu + bivalent COVID today. Pap/HPV 3/2022 neg - next 2027. Mammogram - reordered, due (last 5/2019 outside). Colonoscopy 2029-32. Lipids 8/2021 - repeat 2024-26. Lung cancer screening: not yet eligible (USPSTF from age 50); will start when eligible.
2. Tobacco dependence - relapse. Motivated but not ready to set date now; will reconsider after the holidays. Offered patch/gum anytime.
3. COPD GOLD 2 - stable.
4. Diverticulosis - fiber.
RTC 6 mo.
R. Halvorsen, MD

reports.text:

COMPARISON: Outside study 5/2019, images obtained.
FINDINGS: Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcifications, or architectural distortion.
IMPRESSION: BI-RADS 1: Negative. Routine screening.
D. Moreau, MD, Radiology

patients.summary: Patrol officer and long-time smoker with GOLD 2 COPD who establishes care in 2021 after her Lowell PCP retires; past fertility care with a 2011 miscarriage reaches the chart through outside records. Her course brings COVID-19 on Paxlovid, a screening colonoscopy finding diverticulosis and an adenoma, an exacerbation leading to pulmonology switching her inhaler, two diverticulitis episodes, an incidental lung nodule followed to stability, and a successful 2024 quit.
